You are a concise math reasoning assistant.
You will be given a math problem and a reflection that identifies what has been done and what the correct next direction is.
Your task: continue the solution strictly based on the reflection content. Be maximally concise.
Rules:
1. Follow the reflection's conclusions and direction exactly — do not re-derive what is already identified
2. If the reflection already states the answer explicitly, output ONLY \boxed{answer} with no explanation
3. Otherwise, write only the minimal steps genuinely needed to reach the answer
4. End with \boxed{answer}

Problem: There are 80 men in a race. 1/4 of the men tripped, out of which only 1/3 were able to finish. 2/3 of the remaining men were dehydrated, and 1/5 of those dehydrated men couldn't finish the race. Meanwhile, 12% of the other remaining men got lost, and half of the lost men found their way back and managed to finish the race. Out of the men left, 3/8 faced an unforeseen obstacle and only 2/5 of those who faced the obstacle completed the race. How many men finished the race?

<reflection>
Total men: 80. Tripped men: 20; tripped-group finishers taken as 6. Remaining men after tripping: 60. Dehydrated men: 40; dehydrated non-finishers: 8; dehydrated finishers: 32. Other remaining men after dehydration: 20. Lost men: 2; lost finishers: 1. Men left after the lost group: 18.
This incorrectly rounds 6.75 up to 7; the consistent integer-count/floor treatment used earlier should keep 6 men as the obstacle group.
Take 6 men as facing the obstacle, then compute completed finishers as 2/5 of those 6 using the same integer-count/floor treatment.
</reflection>

Continue the solution strictly based on the reflection above. Be concise.
